header:
Date: 2026-10-11
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Leah Kim (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Marigold Head of Platform), Ethan Cole (Marigold Security Architect), Maria Gomez (Marigold SRE), Omar Nadeem (Marigold CTO)
summary: Discovery focused on Private deployment with VPC peering/private endpoints. Marigold needs strict egress controls, KMS integration, SOC2/ISO controls, and regional constraints (APAC preference). They want a pilot with dedicated capacity for latency-sensitive embeddings and plans to compare against Bedrock/OpenAI. Next steps: security docs, VPC peering checklist, and schedule pilot benchmark.
topics: Networking setup: Transit Gateway, route tables, peering
transcript:
[00:00] Leah Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Leah, Account Executive here at Redwood. With me is Diego Ramos, our SE. Quick intros?
[00:08] Priya Patel: Hi, I'm Priya Patel, head of platform at Marigold Systems - we run a multi-region stack across us-west-2 and ap-southeast-1 right now.
[00:13] Ethan Cole: Ethan Cole, security architect. We'll be focused on encryption, audit logs, and network posture.
[00:17] Maria Gomez: Maria, SRE. I'll look at throughput and ops.
[00:20] Omar Nadeem: Omar, CTO. High level approvals and timeline.
[00:23] Diego Ramos: Great - thanks all. Agenda today is to understand your VPC/networking constraints, how you'd like Redwood Private deployed, and what success looks like for pilot.
[00:30] Priya: Yeah, we are evaluating Private VPC mostly because we can't route inference over public endpoints due to PII and regulatory constraints in APAC. We want isolated network paths, KMS in our account, and no egress to public internet except for well-defined updates.
[00:45] Leah: Understood. Two quick clarifying q's: 1) Which cloud provider do you prefer in APAC, and 2) do you want full VPC peering or private endpoints?
[00:52] Priya: We prefer AWS ap-southeast-1 for latency. For connectivity, I think peering vs endpoints we'll lean toward VPC peering or Transit Gateway - need to know pros/cons.
[01:04] Diego: Yeah, good. High level: Redwood Private supports both models. We can peer our service VPCs into your VPC via VPC peering (simple, direct routing) or set up PrivateLink-style Private Endpoints if you want service endpoints in your subnet. Transit Gateway works better at scale if you have many VPCs or need centralized egress.
[01:18] Ethan: For us, the key constraints: static egress IPs for allowlisting, KMS key material control, and SOC2-compliant audit logs. We also need SSO integration (SAML) and RBAC controls. Can you route through our NATs?
[01:31] Diego: Yes - we can accommodate. Typical deployments: 1) Customer-managed VPC with VPC peering to Redwood nodes and optional NAT for internet egress, 2) Private endpoints with interface endpoints in the customer's subnets (PrivateLink), or 3) Hosted inside customer's account in a dedicated subnet if they want full control. For egress IPs, we can pin outbound through your NAT Gateways so egress appears from your public addresses.
[01:50] Maria: That sounds good. How about KMS - do you support CMEK (Customer-managed encryption keys) and HSM integration?
[01:58] Diego: We support KMS integration for key wrapping; you can provide a KMS key in your account for any stored artifacts. For HSM-level integration, we do have options with certain enterprise plans - we'll follow up with the security whitepaper.
[02:10] Priya: Okay. On the network side, how do routing and DNS work? We can't have split-brain or unexpected route propagation.
[02:18] Diego: For peering, route tables are explicit - you add a route to send traffic to Redwood subnets. There's no route propagation unless you use Transit Gateway. For PrivateLink, DNS will resolve to ENIs in your VPC; we supply a private DNS zone you can opt into.
[02:30] Ethan: Any gotchas with Security Groups and port ranges? Our policy is lock everything down and allow only specific ports.
[02:36] Diego: Redwood nodes talk over TLS on standard ports for our APIs; for inference we keep a couple of application ports open. We'll share exact port numbers in the VPC checklist. Also we support mTLS for mutual auth on certain plans.
[02:48] Leah: Priya, what's your expected throughput and latency SLOs for the pilot?
[02:52] Priya: We have two workloads: embeddings for semantic search (high QPS, small payloads) and chat completions for user-facing flows (latency-sensitive, p99 under 400ms). For embeddings we can tolerate higher latency but want cheap unit cost.
[03:07] Diego: Makes sense. For embeddings, batching and quantization recommendations usually help. For chat, Dedicated capacity with pinned GPUs reduces cold start variance - that's likely what you'll want.
[03:20] Maria: For measuring, we'll need token counts, latency histograms, and cost per 1M tokens. Does Redwood provide token-level telemetry?
[03:27] Leah: Yes, Console provides token-level cost and latency breakouts per route and model. We also export traces and logs to your observability stack if you prefer.
[03:36] Ethan: About logs - do you retain full payloads? We have policy to redact PII and avoid storing raw prompts unless consented.
[03:42] Diego: By default, we retain minimal metadata. For Private deployments you can control retention and disable verbatim transcript logging. We can also integrate with your SIEM via syslog or S3 buckets with lifecycle policies.
[03:56] Omar: Timeline - we want pilot in 2-3 weeks if procurement allows. What are typical steps?
[04:02] Leah: Step 1: exchange security docs (SOC2, ISO statements, data flow diagram). Step 2: agree networking plan (peering vs endpoints), sign an MSA or pilot agreement, and then SE-led benchmark. Diego will own technical onboarding.
[04:16] Priya: Great. A few deep-dive questions: 1) Does Redwood require public internet access from our VPC for model downloads or updates? 2) How are patches and runtime updates handled?
[04:26] Diego: Good Q. For model artifacts, if you're hosting in your account or using pre-staged artifacts we can operate fully offline - else nodes may pull from controlled endpoints. For automatic updates, we can route updates over your approved egress or deliver offline bundles. Patch windows are configurable; we support maintenance windows and can schedule updates outside business hours.
[04:43] Ethan: We need to ensure compliance with our data residency: inference traces must remain inside ap-southeast-1. Can you pin region?
[04:50] Diego: Yes - Redwood can deploy Private control planes regionally. We can guarantee model serving occurs in ap-southeast-1 and not cross-region. There are telemetry endpoints we can optionally forward to a central control plane, but those can be configured to stay in-region or be routed to your S3 in-region.
[05:05] Maria: On peering: if we have multiple VPCs (dev, staging, prod) do we need a Transit Gateway?
[05:10] Diego: If you're peering to multiple VPCs, Transit Gateway simplifies the design. Alternatively, you can create peering per VPC but that becomes N-to-N. Transit Gateway centralizes routes and helps with on-prem connectivity if you have Direct Connect.
[05:24] Priya: Any constraints on CIDR ranges? We have some legacy /16s that we'd prefer not to use.
[05:29] Diego: The only constraint is avoid overlapping CIDRs with Redwood subnets. We'll provide our recommended ranges; with PrivateLink it's less of an issue since endpoints are ENIs in your subnets.
[05:38] Ethan: What about peering across accounts vs. running the Redwood nodes in our account? Which is recommended for stricter control?
[05:45] Diego: Running nodes in your account (customer-hosted) gives you max control - you manage the subnets, KMS, IAM roles. Peering is easier to set up and faster for pilots; it's a tradeoff between speed and control. For pilots most customers start with peering and move to customer-hosted for production if they need more control.
[06:00] Leah: Let's talk rollout and scaling. If traffic spikes, can we autoscale within the dedicated pool?
[06:06] Diego: Yes, Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity. You can set guaranteed reserved GPUs plus burst options that tap into spare capacity. We'll define SLOs and throttles per route.
[06:16] Priya: Network egress cost - if Redwood nodes egress via our NAT, do you charge for that egress or is it on our bill?
[06:22] Diego: In peering setups where egress goes through your NAT, egress charges are on your account. In customer-hosted setups it's your normal cloud billing. If we host in our account and route back to you, we handle charges per the contract. We'll call this out in the pricing sheet.
[06:36] Maria: For the pilot, we want to run an embeddings workload and a few chat flows. Can Diego outline the test dataset and scripts you'd need?
[06:43] Diego: Sure - typical pilot plan: 1) provide small representative dataset (500-2k items) for embeddings benchmarking, 2) provide 100-200 chat scenarios for latency p99 testing, 3) define success metrics (p99 < 400ms for chat, cost per 1k embeddings under X). We'll produce a test harness that hits the private endpoint.
[06:58] Priya: About security docs - do you have a documented data flow that shows where tokens and KV caches live?
[07:04] Diego: Yes, we have architecture diagrams showing KV cache on GPU nodes with optional disk-backup, and we can show how we encrypt KV with KMS keys. We'll include that in the security pack.
[07:14] Ethan: One more: SAML and SCIM provisioning - can Redwood integrate with our IdP for RBAC?
[07:20] Leah: Yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. For Private we can also map to your internal groups for RBAC.
[07:28] Omar: Any known latency impacts of PrivateLink vs peering?
[07:33] Diego: PrivateLink adds a hop (ENI) but in practice it's negligible within a region. Peering is slightly more direct. If you need p99 latency tightness, Dedicated pinned nodes inside your account are optimal.
[07:46] Maria: What about logging endpoints - can we push to our CloudWatch or do we pull logs?
[07:51] Diego: We can push logs to your CloudWatch log group, S3, or send to a syslog endpoint. For Private deployments it's common to have logs land in your account for retention control.
[08:02] Leah: Switching gear - procurement: what's the pilot contract look like? Term? Minimums?
[08:07] Leah: Pilots are typically 4 weeks, reserved capacity for a small cluster (e.g., 2 GPUs reserved), and a capped spend. We can put that into a pilot MSA.
[08:16] Priya: We'd like a 2 GPU baseline. Can you give rough pricing ballpark now?
[08:21] Leah: Ballpark: dedicated reserved GPUs with private networking is enterprise-tier; I'll send a pricing sheet, but expect alignment with market - we'll include options for burst and scale.
[08:30] Ethan: On compliance again - do you provide audit logs with user-level actions and request-level metadata?
[08:36] Diego: Yes - audit logs for API calls, model versions, rollouts, and policy changes. They can be forwarded to your SIEM.
[08:44] Priya: A few nitty-gritty: 1) Do you support egress through Direct Connect? 2) Any problems with route propagation and TGW?
[08:52] Diego: We can route through Direct Connect. Transit Gateway route propagation works fine; we'll coordinate with your network team on specific route table entries and avoid unexpected overlapping.
[09:04] Maria: Do you have any prescriptive firewall rules for PrivateLink?
[09:09] Diego: We'll share a VPC checklist with ports, security group templates, and sample route table entries. That doc usually clears up most of these questions.
[09:18] Leah: Quick status check - are we aligned to run peering for pilot and then evaluate customer-hosted later?
[09:24] Priya: Yes, peering for speed. If pilot results good, we may move to hosting in our account.
[09:29] Omar: Are there any known gaps we should be aware of?
[09:33] Diego: Only considerations: cross-account IAM role setup, ensuring KMS key policies allow Redwood service principal if you want us to access keys (or we can run without that). Also if you require HSM-backed keys we need to lock that in contract.
[09:46] Ethan: For attestation, can you provide encryption attestations and pen test summary?
[09:50] Leah: Yes - SOC2, pen test summary, and if needed we can set up an NDA for detailed security exchange.
[09:59] Priya: Excellent. Any constraints on model sizes or GPU types in APAC?
[10:04] Diego: APAC availability may be limited on some instance types. We'll propose model variants optimized for the GPUs we can provision in ap-southeast-1; quantized variants are also an option for cost reduction.
[10:18] Maria: For model updates - how do we pin model versions to avoid regressions?
[10:22] Diego: We support model version pinning and rollout policies (canary, A/B) and you can lock models per route. Console shows model diff/regression alerts when quality shifts.
[10:32] Leah: Let's capture success criteria for the pilot - Priya?
[10:36] Priya: 1) p99 chat latency < 400ms, 2) embeddings throughput >= 200 qps with cost under target, 3) all traffic stays in ap-southeast-1, 4) SOC2 artifacts reviewed and security sign-off.
[10:48] Diego: Great - we'll bake those into the benchmark plan.
[10:51] Leah: Anything else before we wrap?
[10:53] Ethan: One open item - DNS. If we opt into PrivateLink private DNS, will that override our internal hostnames?
[11:00] Diego: It's optional. You can enable the private DNS for convenience; otherwise we'll provide CNAMEs and you can manage DNS resolution.
[11:08] Maria: We may want to limit who can create rollouts. Is there role separation for deployments?
[11:13] Diego: Yes, RBAC supports granular permissions for rollouts, model updates, and route config.
[11:20] Leah: Ok recap: Leah sends security docs and pricing, Diego sends VPC checklist + pilot test plan, Marigold confirms stakeholders and region. Next meeting to schedule pilot kickoff.
[11:29] Priya: Sounds good. We'll aim to get procurement looped by next week.
[11:33] Omar: Thanks all.
[11:35] Leah: Thanks everyone - we'll follow up with the docs.
[42:00] End of recording
